notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is "unavailable" in per_rule. Runs were made at 58f6318 with the uncommitted rule changes (skill_hash 9faec678...).

Method and mapping are the previous grade's: 15 rules, 20 planted problems; a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or the finding's stated fix addresses it, and a silent fix in the improved code does not count; a rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported or the improved code still contains it, else clean. The 10-40 nesting row belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 32 and 36,39 to 'Match every expected shape'; the comments and both magic numbers to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise and the 10-40 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; lines 12 and 51 to the pipeline rule; line 21 is_binary to no rule. A one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body (haiku-1 line 78, haiku-2 line 84, sonnet-1 line 65, sonnet-2 line 61) is not nesting, and a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` (haiku-1 line 97, haiku-2 line 110, sonnet-2 line 103) is not counted, as before. A magic number counts as reported only if a finding names it or its fix names it with an attribute, so a fix that keeps the literal does not count, as in the baseline.

Bare-struct insert (planted lines 22-24): 4 of 4 runs reported it (haiku-1 finding 7, haiku-2 finding 4, sonnet-1 finding 10, sonnet-2 finding 4), and 0 of 4 improved modules still insert a bare struct; all four go through an assumed User changeset. In the previous sweep's four haiku and sonnet runs, 1 of 4 reported it and 3 of 4 still inserted a bare `%User{}`.

'Validate input with changesets' changed since 93873be and is graded against the current text; the sentence that now decides it is "A `%User{}` built from the params and passed to `Repo.insert/1` or `Repo.update/1` is the pattern to replace: Ecto writes the struct as given, so nothing is validated and a constraint violation raises." (idiomatic-elixir/references/ecto-phoenix.md, ## Validate input with changesets). The previous standard on hand checks is kept: an assumed `User.changeset/2` with validation counts as clean even when fields are also parsed by hand (haiku-1 line 96, haiku-2 line 116).

Naming is not in this case's rule list, so it can only appear in other_violations. Its fetch sentence now reads "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming). No run names a `fetch_*` function: sonnet-1 uses `string_field/2`, and sonnet-2 uses `string_field/2` and `integer_field/2`, saying in finding 13 that they are named by job because they return error reasons. In the previous sweep, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 were listed under other_violations for `fetch_email/1`, `fetch_age/1`, `fetch_role/1`; here 0 of 4.

The `with` rule is not in this case's list either. Its one-step paragraph now reads "With one step there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps. Use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place:" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function). Sonnet-1 line 87 is a one-step `with`, listed under other_violations. Haiku-2's `import_user_id/2` uses `case` (lines 95-98). The previous grade did not list the one-step `with` in previous haiku-1 line 71 and haiku-2 line 81 under the old sentence "Use `case` when there is only one step."

SKILL.md's reference-file bullet now says "read every reference file whose trigger appears in the code or the task, before you write code and, in a review, before you list findings" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## How to use this skill). reads: haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 are each ["SKILL.md", "ecto-phoenix.md", "processes.md"], confirmed in the transcripts, and in each transcript both reference reads come before the Write of review.md (sonnet-2 read both with `cat` in one Bash call). In the previous sweep, sonnet-2 skipped ecto-phoenix.md.

Judgment calls on 'reported': haiku-1's line 21 is_binary counts through finding 9's fix ("inside a function that checks the input is a binary first"). Haiku-2's line 8 raise counts through finding 15's fix (per-field functions returning `{:error, {:missing_field, key}}` for lines 6-13), although the finding says missing fields fail "with a generic error" and does not single out the role. Haiku-2's lines 36,39 count through finding 15, sonnet-1's through finding 3's fix ("with explicit error reasons"), and sonnet-2's through findings 2 and 6. Sonnet-2's line 12 counts through the last sentence of finding 12.

False positives on line 26: haiku-1 finding 10 and sonnet-1 finding 6 apply the `and`/`or`/`not` rule to `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]`. Both count, as the previous grade counted haiku-2 finding 12, whose fix also said the line goes away.

Two new verdict calls. (1) Both haiku runs say the line 11 why-comment stays (haiku-1 finding 16, haiku-2 finding 14), but their improved code drops it. Comments is graded violated because the rule says "Keep comments that explain a reason the code cannot show." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Comments explain why; documentation goes in `@moduledoc` and `@doc`), as the baseline grade did for baseline-haiku-2. This is the only basis for both haiku Comments verdicts; under the planted-problem mapping alone, both would be clean. (2) Sonnet-1 lines 87-88 put a multi-line `case` inside a `with`. 'Keep functions short' is graded violated under "When a `case`, `if`, or `with` appears inside another one, move the inner one into a named private function."; the one-line-`if` exemption does not cover it.

Not flagged, to match the previous grade: haiku-2 reads keys with `params["email"]` and `params["age"]` (lines 80-81) and adds `nil` clauses (lines 101, 105), the pattern 'Parse external data into structs where it enters the system' describes and its own finding 15 cites. The previous grade did not flag the same construct in previous haiku-2.
